title: Choose the visual world
question: Which direction should guide the portfolio redesign? Choose a card, ask for a fresh hand, or take the category standard.

options.label: The Cutaway Folio
options.lineage: Architectural sectional drawings and exploded studies
options.thesis: A vivid section drawing makes your profile, technical range, and product-building approach read as one connected practice.
options.viewport: One connected cutaway composition integrates your portrait, name, role, exact current profile copy, and verified technologies; labeled interface, application, and backend planes lead into the real work section below.
options.risk: Without published case studies, the diagram can explain your range but cannot prove shipped outcomes.

raised.raise: Layer focus has a visible purpose: selecting a verified skill group brings its real labels forward and lets the others recede.
A simple, readable section index keeps the visitor oriented as the visual field changes.
Every interaction has a clear labeled state; color supports the state but never carries it alone.
One oversized callout at a time points to a real profile fact or current technology, with deliberate negative space around it.
One typographic scale shift gives the profile a decisive focal moment while all supporting copy stays comfortably readable.

options.label: The Engineering Journal
options.lineage: Independent engineering journals and printed technical indexes
options.thesis: A current issue of your working practice: direct, exact, and energized by the details.
options.viewport: The opening spread gives your name and role a strong editorial lead, with the current profile, exact skill inventory, and a compact process index arranged as one authored page.
options.risk: Editorial portfolios are familiar in this category, so the page needs an unusually strong focal composition to feel personal.

options.label: The Unfolding Systems Sheet
options.thesis: Your real skills and approach unfold from one precise sheet instead of being split into generic cards.
options.viewport: A single unfolding sheet introduces your profile and opens into clearly labeled technology groups; the beginning of Selected work sits on the next fold.
options.case: Strong audience fit for engineering-minded visitors and a memorable systems metaphor; loses to the cutaway on plain-language product clarity.
options.risk: If the fold mechanics lead too strongly, visitors may remember the motion before your actual work and skills.

options.label: Floated Pigment
options.thesis: The content becomes a one-off fluid drawing.
options.viewport: A profile and skill labels set inside a changing pigment field.
options.case: The art process outshines the professional profile and gives the visitor little help reading the technology range.
options.kept: Each interaction should visibly change a real content layer.
options.risk: Fluid marks can hide text and turn the portfolio into an art demo.

options.label: The Cutting Bench
options.thesis: The portfolio reads as a rail of film frames.
options.viewport: Profile and skills appear as frames across a single scrub rail.
options.case: The editing tool is an imposed metaphor, and there is no verified footage or case-study sequence to carry its structure.
options.kept: Keep the visitor oriented with a stable index as the story moves.
options.risk: Scrubbing may make a straightforward portfolio harder to navigate.

options.label: The Kiln Shelf
options.lineage: Glaze tests on a ceramic kiln shelf
options.thesis: The page tracks color as it flows and hardens.
options.viewport: Profile facts sit beside a row of vivid glaze samples.
options.case: Ceramic test states do not connect to the real content, while sample recipes suggest unprovided process evidence.
options.kept: Interaction states should remain distinct and easy to read.
options.risk: The metaphor could imply projects and experiments that are not in the source data.

options.label: Gyaru Magazine Spread
options.thesis: Profile and technology names crowd together in an expressive spread.
options.viewport: Your portrait anchors a densely annotated profile page.
options.case: The visual language points to fashion and consumer pricing rather than software product work, and the density competes with the facts.
options.kept: A precise, oversized callout can give one real fact a memorable moment.
options.risk: Overlapping elements may make the page look noisy instead of deliberately expressive.

options.label: Copy-Shop Zine
options.thesis: A single column of argument takes over the page.
palette: one changing paper color per sheet
options.viewport: A large typographic profile introduces an annotated technical index below.
options.case: The voice and copy-shop texture make this feel like a personal manifesto instead of an experienced product developer's portfolio.
options.kept: One carefully placed typography shift can carry energy without shrinking reading size.
options.risk: The zine language may read as intentionally rough when the goal is confident craft.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished, expected developer portfolio with a clear profile, work index, and contact path.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional profile header, verified stack labels, clear project and experience empty states, and a direct contact action in the first screen.
canonCard.risk: It will be immediately legible but familiar beside other developer portfolios.
